name: Evelyn Kaur
life: “I still remember a celebration too loud for the person we were welcoming.” People around Paper & Pine Books know Evelyn by a small Wednesday habit. Evelyn starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I argued for a homecoming party until he asked for one evening when nobody wanted a speech.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an old plum windbreaker and a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. Evelyn has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Evelyn raises one eyebrow long before saying yes during a conversation.
personality: Evelyn can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Evelyn can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To give the returning man a speech-free evening.
family: Max Carbone is Evelyn’s half-sibling. Evelyn asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Max remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *Home with stairs*, Max says, “I wanted the bed free for another patient. I went to see the stairs before asking for a date again.”
connections: Frankie Levin. A furniture number and a quiet evening may be more usable than a homecoming party.

reactions.situation: The returning father asks to visit the old address
reactions.response: Evelyn checks whether the person living there now wants visitors.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Evelyn asks the driver to come back on foot and look at the damaged goods before discussing cost.
